@RobertMeisner Ok :smile:

To me it sounds like there are a few changes that need to happen for hasOne (and belongsTo to some degree)
1. HasOne should be using `LEFT JOIN` instead of `INNER JOIN`.
2. When the foreign key is NULL, or the association's data was not found, no entity should be constructed. Having a blank entity also causes #3806. The empty 'not new' entity is also why primary key errors are being emitted.
3. Table::patchEntity() should build the associated record if the post data contains the correct data.

> When the foreign key is NULL, or the association's data was not found, no entity should be constructed. Having a blank entity also causes #3806. The empty 'not new' entity is also why primary key errors are being emitted.

This is somewhat of a unfinished idea, but I would prefer if we still hydrated the empty entities. I find having objects representing a null state more helpful than plain null, specially because you can provide defaults for missing data. I would suggest either adding some info to the entity so it know it was hydrated from empty values or maybe hydrate a different class.

Having the entity there but nulled out makes validation more tricky though. Figuring out whether or not you have to validate data becomes a bit more complicated.

Not having an entity at all makes the decision easy, and makes it really clear at runtime that the data is missing.

It could make validation have an extra step, but I really think that having nulls is something difficult to deal with most of the time. Maybe we could make it configurable at the association level, to either hydrate null entity or just leave it null.
I really don't like configuration for these kinds of things. This feels like the kind of thing the framework should have an opinion on and make its opinion work cohesively.
:+1:  for NULL, if it doesnt exist it doesnt exist. seems intuitive. primaryKey===null seems to me like a bad design.
